matched.actualTitle: SQL Injection via Null Byte Bypass (%00) and SQL Injection with Information Disclosure in /api/search Endpoint
matched.matchReason: Both findings identify SQL injection vulnerability in the /api/search endpoint where user input is concatenated directly into SQL queries without parameterization. The actual findings provide specific bypass techniques (null byte, quote injection, OR-based injection) that demonstrate the underlying SQL injection vulnerability.

matched.expectedTitle: WAF Rule Enumeration - MySQL Version Comment Bypass
matched.actualTitle: WAF Bypass - Ineffective SQL Injection Protection
matched.matchReason: Both findings relate to WAF bypass techniques. While the expected finding specifically mentions MySQL version comments and the actual finding demonstrates case variation and quote repositioning bypasses, they both identify that the WAF has insufficient pattern matching and can be bypassed through various obfuscation techniques on SQL injection attempts.

matched.expectedTitle: Content-Type Confusion for Body Inspection Bypass
matched.actualTitle: Type Confusion Vulnerability - Integer Email Field Causes SQL Error Disclosure and Type Confusion Vulnerability - Integer Password Causes Python Error Disclosure
matched.matchReason: Both relate to content/type confusion attacks on the login endpoint. The actual findings demonstrate type confusion by sending non-string types (integers, booleans) in JSON body parameters, causing application crashes. This aligns with the expected finding's concept of parsing mismatches between WAF/application when different content handling mechanisms are used.

matched.actualTitle: Type Confusion Vulnerability findings and Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint
matched.matchReason: While not a direct parameter pollution example, the actual findings on the login endpoint demonstrate parsing mismatches between what the WAF expects and what the application actually processes. The type confusion findings show that the application handles inputs differently than strict WAF validation would, achieving a similar bypass effect.

matched.expectedTitle: Content-Type Confusion for Body Inspection Bypass
matched.actualTitle: Verbose Error Message Disclosure - Backend Information Exposure
matched.matchReason: Both findings relate to inspection bypass and information disclosure. The actual verbose error messages demonstrate that detailed backend information leaks when bypasses are successful, supporting the concept that WAF inspection can be evaded and sensitive information exposed.

missed.title: WAF Rule Enumeration - MySQL Version Comment Bypass
missed.reason: No evidence of MySQL version comment bypass (/*!50000UNION*/ syntax) was discovered. The actual findings show WAF bypasses using case variation and quote repositioning instead. The target appears to use PostgreSQL (as revealed in error messages), not MySQL, making this specific bypass technique potentially irrelevant to the application environment.

missed.title: Host Header Routing to Internal Admin Panel
missed.reason: No testing or findings related to Host header manipulation to access internal admin panels were reported. The pentest did not identify or attempt to access an admin.internal panel through Host header routing attacks.

missed.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Admin Health Check
missed.reason: No findings related to SSRF vulnerabilities in an /api/health-check endpoint were discovered. While the pentest attempted to find valid credentials to access authenticated endpoints, no SSRF testing on admin panel endpoints was documented.

extra.title: SQL Injection via Null Byte Bypass (%00)
extra.assessment: Valid and significant new discovery. This is a specific SQL injection bypass technique using null bytes that truncates query processing. While the general SQL injection in /api/search was expected, this specific null byte bypass vector and its mechanism is a valuable technical discovery not explicitly mentioned in expected findings.

extra.title: Type Confusion Vulnerability - Integer Email Field Causes SQL Error Disclosure
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery. This specific type confusion attack via integer values in JSON is a detailed technical finding that demonstrates the broader parsing mismatch concept. The information disclosure aspect about PostgreSQL database structure is a critical side-effect discovery.

extra.title: Type Confusion Vulnerability - Integer Password Causes Python Error Disclosure
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery. Similar to the email type confusion, this reveals specific Python implementation details (.encode() method) through type confusion attacks. These findings provide valuable reconnaissance information about the backend stack.

extra.title: Verbose Error Message Disclosure - Backend Information Exposure
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery. While related to the type confusion findings, this is properly identified as a separate information disclosure vulnerability. It systematically documents how the application leaks sensitive backend information (PostgreSQL, Python, database schema) through error messages.

extra.title: Unable to Locate Valid Test Credentials for Authenticated IDOR Testing
extra.assessment: Valid testing limitation. This documents that IDOR testing on the /api/profile endpoint could not be completed due to inability to obtain valid credentials. This is not a new vulnerability but rather a documented testing constraint that prevented evaluation of expected authenticated endpoints.

extra.title: Null Byte Injection in Email Field - Information Disclosure
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery. This specific null byte injection technique in the email parameter reveals backend validation mechanisms. While related to the broader type confusion findings, this documents a distinct attack vector with asymmetric behavior compared to the password field.

extra.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint Enables Brute Force Attacks
extra.assessment: Valid and critical new discovery. The absence of rate limiting, account lockout, or CAPTCHA on the login endpoint enables brute force attacks. This is a significant security finding not mentioned in the expected findings but represents a real and exploitable vulnerability.

extra.title: WAF Bypass - Ineffective SQL Injection Protection
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery. While WAF bypass was expected, this finding documents specific ineffective patterns and successful bypasses on the /api/products endpoint, complementing the SQL injection findings on /api/search with evidence of WAF weaknesses across multiple endpoints.
